label: batch-21
tail:
Batch 21 is **authored with four items marked ready and five escalated**. I added both draft pages, nine item carriers, source coverage, proof contracts, cross-batch evidence, and batch notes.

The main open mathematical work is the local proof of the empirical-Bayes maximizer bracket and the coverage and undercoverage results that depend on it. I retained those claims and recorded proposed A-page suppliers for the missing score-process and blockwise bounds; I did not present the source citations as completed proofs.

The plan conflicts are recorded in the [batch notes](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/bayesian-computational-statistics-62-batch-21.notes.md): the design omits the source’s `theta_{0,1}=0` hypothesis and uses `rho_j` where the source’s sparse-gap theorem uses `rho_{j+1}`. The carriers include the first-coordinate hypothesis and use the source’s growth index. [SVVZ 2015](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.4489v5) also shows why the first-coordinate restriction matters; the unresolved bracket proof involves score-process bounds treated in [Knapik et al. 2012](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1209.3628).

Scoped item dependency levels, proof layout, precheck, rendering, strict proof contracts, citation fidelity, coverage, source-fetch, focused depcheck, and content-policy checks passed. The batch dependency check remains blocked: the assignment says level 0 with no prerequisites, while the current manifests recompute batch 21 at level 5 through batch 9. I left the shared scheduling artifact unchanged. The batch 9 page dependency is recorded as open in the [cross-batch evidence](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/bayesian-computational-statistics-62-batch-21.cross-batch-dependencies.json).

A wording correction to the sparse-gap example was made after its escalation record was written. I left that record escalated and did not overwrite it.
